- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast bias by 5–10% below historical mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 7-day high), model often overshoots; cap forecast peak at 1.2x prior high or 1.5x 14-day moving average.
- In mean-reversion regimes (sentiment neutral to slightly positive), model underestimates recovery; add 2–5% upward bias to 30-day forecast tail.
- If sentiment turns positive after prolonged negative streak, model delays response; shift forecast upward by 3–7% in first 5 days of sentiment shift.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underpredicts downward moves in low-sentiment periods; apply 3–8% upward adjustment for 10–15 day windows with sentiment < -0.4.
- Avoid overfitting to recent 18-day history; if forecast diverges >15% from 30-day moving average, reweight recent data by 50% and use sentiment as decay factor.
